items.title: Share your setup
items.summary: 0.4.1 lets you send one of your loadouts to Player Setups from Configs, and fixes what going over 0.4.0 turned up on Metal, in voice chat and in the launcher.

items.title: The game draws with Metal
items.summary: 0.4.0 moves the game from OpenGL to Metal. OpenGL stays as a choice in Settings, and Display gains a render scale for 4K and 5K screens.

items.title: A tidier launcher
items.summary: 0.3.7 gives every page the same titles, labels, buttons and switches. Nothing in the game changed.

items.title: CoD2 Silicon is now CoD2 Unbound
items.summary: 0.3.6 has the new name and a new icon. From CoD2 Silicon, download it once by hand; your settings come along.

items.title: Your Steam copy, downloaded in setup
items.summary: 0.3.5 can download Call of Duty 2 from Steam during setup: scan a QR code with the Steam app, and nothing about your account is typed.

items.title: Crash reports, if you want them
items.summary: 0.3.4 adds a switch in Settings › Privacy that sends crash reports to the project. It is off until you turn it on.

items.title: A new home at github.com/cod2unbound
items.summary: 0.3.3 follows the project to its organisation. From 0.3.2 or earlier, download it once by hand.

items.title: A console you can read on a 4K or 6K screen
items.summary: 0.3.2 enlarges the in-game console above 1080 lines.

items.title: Friends on Windows can join your CoD2x server
items.summary: 0.3.1 runs as the released CoD2x 1.4.6.8, so nothing needs setting.

next.title: CoD2 Unbound for Windows
next.summary: Next on the roadmap, then Linux. These are plans, not promises.
